correctness.rationale: The adjacent-binomial identity and gcd(bn+1,n)=1 settle all odd-prime factors and the cases of odd bn+1. For b,n odd it leaves failure iff the Kummer count in (4n-1)+(bn+1) is at most one. With h the largest positive odd integer at most nu2(b+3), the sum mod 2^h is n. Here is an independent proof of minimality for h>=3: write n_h=1+sum of 2^j over odd j=1,...,h-2. An odd n<n_h has a first missing bit j in that odd chain. The first summand has bit 1 at j (at j=1 directly, otherwise this is the previous odd bit of n), whereas the output bit is 0. A carry-out is forced there, even if an incoming carry exists. If there is only one carry, the next digit j+1 has output 1 and no carry-out; this 1 propagates along the even positions because bit i of 4n-1 agrees with bit i-2 of n for i>=3. Hence n has its bit h-1 set, contradicting n<n_h<2^(h-1). For h=1 the earlier-index claim is vacuous. At n_h the low h bits are disjoint; the high addition is 1+(qn_h-1), q=(b+3)/2^h, with exactly nu2(q)<=1 carries. The distinct thresholds are realized by b=1 and b=2^h-3 for odd h>=3. An independent Euclidean-quotient recurrence also reproduced the frozen 4- and 11-state certificate, its two-step closure, and its acceptance criterion: python /workspace/review-work/check-fourfold.py. That is an exact finite certificate for an unbounded claim, not an extrapolation.
